observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The instructor talks directly to the camera to explain origins and counts, then switches to a first-person or side-angle view of his feet to demonstrate the steps. He breaks down each variant step-by-step from slow to regular speed before demonstrating them with music.

lesson_structure.note: Explanation of what Dabke is and where it is danced
Breakdown of the basic Dabke steps

cues: Kick with right, slide back with left
Step, kick and slide, right, left, and stomp
Hop with your left and your right knee goes up

steps_taught.name: Basic Dabke Steps
steps_taught.description: Six steps walking to the right ending with a kick and stomp.

steps_taught.name: Sab'a
steps_taught.description: Seven steps each featuring a hop and a kick-slide.

steps_taught.name: Midwaz
steps_taught.description: Faster continuous dabke style with leg crossovers and knee lifts.

what_works: First-person foot camera angle helps viewers follow foot placement directly
Progression from slow explanation to music practice
what_hinders: Frequent camera angle changes between upper body and feet

quotes.text: Dabke is a traditional dance done in the Middle East
The dabke that I'm going to teach you is called Sab'a which means seven
It's now time to learn an even faster type of dabke called Midwaz

evidence_segments.observation: Instructor demonstrates basic steps walking to the right using a first-person shoe-cam perspective on wooden flooring.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: Full body posture and upper body alignment

evidence_segments.observation: Side profile view of instructor demonstrating kick and slide back movement in shorts and socks.

extraction.distinctive_method: Using a first-person chest-mounted or downward-facing camera angle on his feet so learners see the exact footwork from their own perspective.
